blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines — Cebu City will deploy 553 persons in its initial preparations for the Kalag-Kalag 2026 observance, with traffic management, cemetery clearing, vendor regulation and waste disposal among the measures being lined up prior to the annual influx of cemetery visitors. Kenneth Siasar, chief of staff of Cebu City Mayor Nestor Archival, said during a press conference on Monday, October 19, that the city has begun coordinating with the Cebu City Transportation Office (CCTO), Traffic Management Committee (TMC), Department of Public Services (DPS) and other offices to prepare cemeteries and surrounding roads.
